findings.title: Cutover can pass despite failed health and WAL-push commands
findings.description: `run_health` ignores the subprocess result from `shell()`, then treats the last line of the existing health log as the result. If the check fails before writing a new line, a previous clean `FLAGS archive=0 stale=0` can make the step pass. Similarly, `step_offsite` ignores the push command’s return code and checks remote parity afterward; a failed push can therefore escape detection if the subsequent checks succeed. Check and record each command’s exit status, and ensure health results correspond to the current invocation before declaring success.

findings.title: Lifecycle read failures are misreported as passing in the cutover
findings.description: When `b2_lifecycle.sh` fails, this loop reports a `MISSING ... lifecycle-read` item, which makes `setup-backup --check` non-clean. But `step_check` explicitly allows all `17/tick` items, so it can accept an unreadable lifecycle rule set and proceed with the cutover. The final production step only checks the setup command’s exit status, not whether the output contains lifecycle-read failures. Parse and reject unreadable lifecycle results explicitly; only missing rules should remain informational.
